The dashboard displays investment and credited-interest totals, although the 70% bonus banner is not established as connected to the lending offers. Comments about IOTA and Stellar are personal investment discussion and do not establish a specific purchase request.

opening.argument: The video presents personal judgment and uncertainty, not a promise that viewers will profit. The speaker repeatedly directs people toward independent evaluation: he says, “I always go in and do my own research,” and insists, “you have to put in your own work.” He also openly acknowledges uncertainty when discussing services, saying, “I could be wrong on this.” That language matters: the discussion is framed as personal experience and conditional commentary, with viewers told to investigate projects, teams, and backing themselves. Even the privacy-coin discussion recognizes a possible concern, noting that “there could be some shady business going on there.” A cautious commentator can describe what he personally uses without certifying the safety or profitability of those platforms.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited payout language describes the speaker’s reported experience, but it does not itself establish a guarantee, an instruction to deposit, or deception toward viewers. The registration URL shows an available referral path, not that anyone was required to use it. The surrounding language is explicitly research-oriented and uncertain, so the evidence supports commentary about a risky financial topic at least as well as it supports a deceptive solicitation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings to research do not neutralize the concrete endorsement. The speaker says he is a “big fan” of the platform, reports collecting “1 to 2% daily,” and describes transferring money into its wallet. Those are affirmative promotional claims about a recurring-return arrangement, not merely a warning that viewers should investigate it.

opening.argument: The structure is a walkthrough and educational portfolio review. The speaker explains how to use CoinMarketCap, compare markets against USD or Bitcoin, locate exchanges, and research projects through articles and videos. He tells viewers to “start checking it out every day” and describes reviewing “who’s backing it” and “who the team is.” The video also covers several unrelated coins, market rankings, payment technology, and exchange functionality. That breadth is consistent with demonstrating research and discussing a personal portfolio, rather than making one focused solicitation. The lending platforms appear as items in a broader tour of what the speaker personally holds and how he evaluates cryptocurrency projects.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a walkthrough does not make every subject a solicitation. Much of the material concerns market-capitalization rankings, IOTA, Stellar, OMG, exchanges, and research sources. The prosecution identifies the lending discussion, but it does not show that the video’s overall purpose was a payment request rather than explaining the speaker’s portfolio and research process.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The broad portfolio tour does not erase the specific demonstration of lending participation. The speaker labels HextraCoin a platform “that I lend on,” reports daily collection, and then introduces BitConnect as “very similar” while describing lending funds for platform tokens. A tutorial format can still promote a scam mechanism when its concrete example is recurring-return lending.

opening.argument: The evidence is also compatible with ordinary cryptocurrency services and affiliate-style commerce, not necessarily a scam. The video discusses exchanges and a conversion service, and the supplied frames show a Changelly interface for entering a recipient wallet address, while other frames show ordinary market listings and a social-media page. The description provides referral-formatted links, but a referral link alone does not establish a fraudulent return scheme, a downline, or a required deposit. The material does not prove that viewers were promised profits, asked to surrender credentials, or told that losses were impossible. At most, it documents the speaker’s claimed use of financial platforms and his personal interest in cryptocurrency.

If you're struggling with Coinbase, here's another potential option

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a guaranteed-profit phrase is not decisive when the speaker supplies the mechanism himself: he says he lends on HextraCoin, reports daily returns, and discusses a second similar platform. The referral link is corroborating context, not the sole basis. Ordinary exchange activity elsewhere in the video does not change the lending claims or the stated recurring payouts.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not whether exchanges or merchandise are ordinary services. The central evidence is that the speaker describes transferring money into HextraCoin, calls it lending, and reports daily credited interest. He also presents BitConnect as the same kind of arrangement and discusses expected future payouts. Those statements establish recurring-return lending promotion even without a formal guarantee or downline.
